frontal-orbital-advancement-frontal-boss.summary: Surgery aimed at pushing the brow ridge and upper eye socket forward for a stronger, more projected brow and deeper-set eyes.

quick.overview:
Frontal-orbital advancement, also called frontal bossing, is the goal of moving the brow ridge and upper orbital area forward. The payoff people want is a more prominent, masculine upper face and eyes that look more deep-set under a strong brow.

The nearest documented surgery is facial feminization, which usually reduces the brow ridge by grinding or reshaping bone over the frontal sinus, and brow lifts, which change eyebrow position rather than bone projection. Looksmaxxing forum discussion centres on brow lifts and combined surgery trips; no study of cosmetic advancement in people without a craniofacial condition was found.
quick.how: People pursue this through consultations with craniofacial or facial plastic surgeons, often as part of a larger multi-procedure plan. Brow lifts reposition soft tissue, while bone work reshapes the forehead. Healing takes weeks to months before the final shape is visible.
quick.risks: Cranioplasty-type bone surgery carries risks of improper bone healing, bone fragment movement and cyst formation, and thin sinus walls complicate bone work near the forehead. Outcome data for forehead and orbit procedures are limited. It is major surgery under general anaesthesia, so surgeon experience and a realistic consultation matter.

angle.text: The aim is a more projected brow and forehead, which gives a stronger, more masculine upper face and deeper-set eyes. It works by moving the brow ridge and upper orbit forward, or by repositioning brow tissue. Published surgery covers brow lifts and brow reduction rather than cosmetic advancement.

ogee-curve-analysis.summary: A way of judging the S-shaped line from cheekbone to cheek hollow in photos, used to guide cheek fillers and surgery toward fuller, smoother midface contour.

quick.overview:
The ogee curve is the S-shaped line running from the cheekbone down into the hollow of the mid-cheek. People assess it in front and three-quarter photos to see how well their cheek contour flows, and to decide whether cheek treatments could improve it.

Surgeons describe restoring a smooth ogee curve in midface rejuvenation, and filler papers list it with an oval face, pronounced cheekbones and a defined jawline as aesthetic goals. On looksmax.org it is treated as a feature that separates more attractive faces from average ones; no study has tested that claim.
quick.how: Users photograph their face from the front and three-quarter angles and trace the curve to see where cheekbone projection or midface volume falls short. Findings are then discussed with clinicians, who may use fillers or other midface volume treatments. Forum members also link the curve to cheekbone projection, jaw flare and masseter size.
quick.risks: The analysis itself is only a way of looking at photos. The procedures used to pursue the curve, such as fillers or buccal fat removal, carry their own risks, and forums contain accounts of a self-performed buccal fat removal that went wrong.

angle.text: The ogee curve is the S-shaped line from the cheekbone into the cheek hollow, and a smooth one is a stated goal in filler and midface surgery. People check it in front and three-quarter photos, then use the result to plan cheek volume treatments. Its role in attractiveness comes from forum opinion rather than trials.

canthopexy.summary: Surgery that anchors the outer eyelid tendon to tighten and lift the lower lid without cutting the corner, for a firmer lid line and more almond eye shape.

quick.overview:
Canthopexy anchors the lateral canthal tendon to lift and support the lower eyelid without cutting the lid margin at the outer corner. People look to it for a firmer lower lid and a slightly more lifted, almond-shaped eye, usually as a gentler alternative to canthoplasty.

Surgical papers present it as a routine companion to lower blepharoplasty that restores lid tone and contour and reduces the chance of lid malposition. A 1993 paper argued it should be a routine part of lower lid blepharoplasty, and a 10-year review reported outcomes with routine lateral canthal support.
quick.how: A suture secures the lateral canthal tendon to the orbital rim, giving the lower lid support and a slight outward lift. It is often performed together with lower blepharoplasty. The change is visible once swelling settles. Canthoplasty differs because it cuts the canthus.
quick.risks: Lower lid surgery is associated with lid malposition, and canthal support is used to reduce that risk. Ectropion prevention is itself a studied use. Forum members disagree about how long cosmetic results last, and it is surgery with the usual anaesthesia and healing risks.

angle.text: Canthopexy tightens and repositions the lower eyelid without cutting the outer corner, giving a firmer lid line and a more lifted, almond or fox-eye shape. The change is visible once healed. It is a routine companion to lower blepharoplasty in the surgical literature.

tarsal-strip-procedure.summary: Eyelid surgery that tightens a lax lower lid by anchoring it to the outer eye socket, reducing sagging and visible white below the iris.

quick.overview:
The tarsal strip is an eyelid operation that shortens and re-anchors the outer end of a loose lower lid to the bone of the outer eye socket. People look to it for a tighter, more youthful lower lid and less visible white below the iris (scleral show).

It was described in 1979 for lids that sag, turn outward (ectropion) or turn inward (entropion). Published studies are case series, retrospective reviews and a few randomised trials, mostly on functional eyelid problems and complications after lower blepharoplasty rather than purely cosmetic goals.
quick.how: Surgeons describe the problem as laxity of the lateral canthal tendon. A strip of tarsal plate at the outer lid is freed and fixed to the periosteum of the lateral orbital rim, tightening the lid against the eye. Results show once swelling settles, and the operation is sometimes combined with other eyelid surgery.
quick.risks: Lower-lid surgery carries a risk of lid retraction, scleral show and ectropion, which is why tarsal strip and similar techniques are also used to prevent and treat these problems. Outcomes depend on how lax the lid is beforehand and on surgeon technique.

angle.text: The tarsal strip tightens a lax lower eyelid by anchoring it to the outer orbital rim, reducing sagging and visible white below the iris for a tighter, more youthful lid. The result is visible after healing. It is an established oculoplastic operation studied mainly for lid function.

medial-epicanthoplasty.summary: Surgery that releases or removes the skin fold over the inner eye corner to open the eye and make it look wider.

quick.overview:
Medial epicanthoplasty reduces or removes the epicanthal fold, the skin fold covering the inner corner of the eye. People use it to expose more of the inner corner, lengthen the eye's horizontal opening and change how wide-set the eyes look.

The fold is common in East Asian populations, and the operation is described mainly in Asian blepharoplasty, where it is often combined with double eyelid surgery. Evidence consists of retrospective series, an anatomical study and small trials. On looksmax.org users have discussed it for inner-corner shape, including planning surgery in Korea.
quick.how: Several techniques exist, including Z-plasty, Y-V advancement and skin-redraping methods, each rearranging skin at the inner corner to release the fold. It is frequently done in the same session as double eyelid surgery. The final look appears after swelling and scar maturation.
quick.risks: Scarring at the inner corner is the central concern; a randomised split-face trial tested botulinum toxin to reduce hypertrophic scars after the operation. Recurrence and asymmetry are also reported.

angle.text: Medial epicanthoplasty releases the fold over the inner eye corner so the eye opens up and looks wider. The change is visible once healed and is often paired with double eyelid surgery. It is well described in the Asian blepharoplasty literature, mostly as case series.

double-eyelid-surgery-asian-blepharoplas.summary: Surgery that creates an upper-lid crease for people who lack one, giving more defined, open-looking eyes.

quick.overview:
Double eyelid surgery forms a crease in the upper eyelid for people whose lids lack one. The payoff is a defined lid line and eyes that look larger and more open.

It is among the most popular cosmetic procedures in many East Asian countries, particularly South Korea, with operations typically lasting 30 to 60 minutes. The literature is large but mostly surgical case series, including patient-reported outcome studies such as a FACE-Q validation of 200 cases.
quick.how: Surgeons use incisional approaches, which fix the skin to deeper lid structures through a cut, and suture approaches that use buried stitches. It is often combined with epicanthoplasty. Stitches are typically removed after 5 to 7 days, and the crease settles as swelling goes down.
quick.risks: The literature describes static or overly depressed folds, multiple folds, asymmetry and failed folds that need revision, plus suture-related problems with buried-suture methods.

angle.text: Double eyelid surgery forms an upper-lid crease, giving more lid definition and a larger, more open-looking eye. The result is visible after healing. It is among the most commonly performed cosmetic procedures in East Asia, studied mostly in surgical case series.

non-incisional-double-eyelid-suture-meth.summary: Double eyelid surgery that forms a crease with buried stitches instead of a skin cut, popular across Asia.

quick.overview:
The suture method creates an upper-lid crease by passing buried stitches through the eyelid, tethering skin to deeper tissue without a skin incision. The payoff is a defined double eyelid and a more open-looking eye, with the appeal of no cut.

Surgical papers describe it as one of two main approaches, the other being the incision method, and as very popular in Asia, especially China. Studies are retrospective cohorts and case series that look at how long creases last, reoperation risk by age and fat removal, and eyebrow position changes.
quick.how: Sutures are placed at one or more points (for example two-point or continuous techniques) and buried, creating an adhesion that forms the crease line. The crease is visible soon after the procedure, then settles as swelling goes down.
quick.risks: Because it leaves suture thread in the lid, foreign-material complications must be considered. Reports describe suture exposure causing corneal damage, sometimes initially misdiagnosed, crease loss from suture loosening and reoperation, and suture problems needing removal.

angle.text: The suture method creates an upper-lid crease with buried stitches instead of an incision, giving a defined double eyelid soon after the procedure. It is popular in Asia, especially China. The literature focuses on how long the crease lasts and on suture complications.

ptosis-surgery-levator-advancement.summary: Surgery that lifts a drooping upper eyelid, giving a more open, alert-looking eye as well as better vision.

quick.overview:
Ptosis surgery raises an upper eyelid that sits too low. Beyond vision, people use it for a more open, alert eye, and one looksmax.org member shared a before-and-after account of a bilateral repair.

Levator advancement tightens or reattaches the levator aponeurosis, the tendon that lifts the lid, and is a standard approach for ptosis caused by age or stretching. It was described in the ophthalmic literature in 1979. Evidence consists of case series, anatomy studies and functional-outcome studies.
quick.how: Surgeons choose among levator advancement or resection, Muller muscle-conjunctival resection for milder ptosis, and frontalis sling for severe cases, depending on cause and how well the levator works. The lifted lid is visible after swelling settles.
quick.risks: Reported problems include uneven lids, dry eye, bleeding, infection and, rarely, loss of lid movement. One study cited on Wikipedia found about half of surgical patients needed more surgery within 8 to 10 years. It is mainly a functional operation, so revision and asymmetry are part of the picture.

angle.text: Ptosis repair raises a drooping upper eyelid, producing a more open, alert-looking eye as well as better function. The lifted lid is visible after healing. It is primarily a functional operation supported by medical case series, with appearance benefit discussed by patients and on forums.

oxymetazoline-eye-drops-upneeq.summary: A prescription 0.1% oxymetazoline eye drop approved for acquired ptosis that briefly lifts the upper lid for a more open, awake look.

quick.overview:
Upneeq is oxymetazoline hydrochloride 0.1% ophthalmic solution, approved by the FDA in July 2020 for acquired blepharoptosis in adults. For looks, it gives a brief lift to a mildly drooping upper lid so the eyes appear more open and awake.

Oxymetazoline is an alpha-adrenergic agonist developed in 1961 and long used in nasal decongestant sprays and redness drops. For ptosis it is thought to stimulate receptors in Muller's muscle, which raises the lid. Published case reports also describe it for lid ptosis after botulinum toxin treatment.
quick.how: It is used as a prescription eye drop for a temporary lift that lasts for hours rather than a permanent change. On looksmax.org, users note it is costly and hard to obtain outside the US, and some ask whether nasal spray can substitute; nasal spray is made for the nose and is not the approved eye product.
quick.risks: Nasal oxymetazoline is described as causing rebound congestion and dependence. Clinicians' views on putting nasal spray in the eye are not covered here, and substituting it is not the approved use, so a clinician is the right person to ask.

angle.text: Upneeq is a prescription oxymetazoline eye drop that stimulates the lid muscle to lift a slightly drooping upper lid, so the eyes look more open and awake for a few hours. It is approved for acquired ptosis, and the lift has been studied in ptosis trials. Forum users also discuss nasal-spray substitutes, which are not the approved product.

eyelid-tape-fold-stickers.summary: Thin adhesive strips that press the upper lid into a temporary crease for an instant double eyelid or more open eye.

quick.overview:
Eyelid tape and fold stickers are small, often crescent-shaped adhesive strips placed on the upper lid so the skin folds into a visible crease. People with single (monolid) lids use them for a double eyelid look without surgery, and looksmaxxers also use them to lift hooded or drooping lids.

The effect lasts as long as the strip stays on. Research is limited to a few small studies and reports: a 2020 study looked at the front surface of the eye after four weeks of wear in young women with single eyelids, a case series described tape holding up a drooping lid in myotonic dystrophy type 1, and a 2025 paper reviewed long-term use.
quick.how: The strip sticks to the lid skin and holds a fold above the lash line, imitating the crease a levator attachment forms naturally. It is applied daily, often under or alongside makeup, and removed at night. It is the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery.
quick.risks: Skin irritation from adhesives and repeated lid stretching are the concerns most often mentioned in the cosmetic and plastic surgery literature. Eyelid tape is a cosmetic product sold without prescription in most markets.

angle.text: Eyelid tape and fold stickers create a temporary upper-lid crease, giving a double eyelid look or a more open eye straight away. They are removable and are the non-surgical counterpart to double eyelid surgery. Small studies have looked at effects on the eye surface after weeks of wear.

eyelid-glue.summary: Cosmetic adhesive that sets the upper lid skin into a temporary crease for a double eyelid look that day.

quick.overview:
Eyelid glue is a cosmetic adhesive used to fix the upper lid skin into a fold, producing a temporary double eyelid. The payoff is a visible crease and a larger, more open-looking, defined eye for the day, with no surgery.

It serves the same goal as eyelid tape and is a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery, which creates a permanent crease. No published clinical studies of the glue itself were located.
quick.how: A thin layer of adhesive holds a fold of lid skin in place so a crease shows when the eye is open. It is applied as part of a daily routine, often with makeup, and lasts until it wears off or is removed.
quick.risks: Any adhesive used next to the eye raises general questions of skin and eye irritation, which have not been specifically studied for these products.

angle.text: Eyelid glue holds the lid skin in a fold to give a visible double eyelid crease and larger, more defined eyes for the day. It is used as a non-surgical alternative to double eyelid surgery. Published research on the product itself is limited.

canthal-tilt-tape-lateral-eye-lift-tape.summary: Tape pulled toward the temple to angle the outer eye corners upward for a more tilted, hunter-eye look while worn.

quick.overview:
Canthal tilt tape is adhesive tape stuck near the outer corner of the eye and pulled back toward the temple, so the outer corner sits higher. The payoff is a more upward-angled outer corner, called positive canthal tilt in looksmaxxing, and a sharper, more tilted eye look.

The change in angle is visible straight away and ends when the tape comes off. No published studies of the tape were found.
quick.how: The tape holds the skin at the lateral canthus under tension, intended to raise the apparent position of the outer corner relative to the inner corner. It is worn for the day or for photos and removed afterward.
quick.risks: No studies of safety were found. Adhesive and skin tension near the eye are general considerations, and repeated pulling on delicate eyelid skin may irritate it.

angle.text: Looksmaxxers use canthal tilt tape to lift the outer eye corners for a more upward-angled, positive canthal tilt look while it is worn. The tape pulls the outer corner toward the temple, and the change in angle is visible straight away. No studies on the tape were found.

winged-eyeliner-for-tilt.summary: Extending eyeliner outward and upward past the outer corner to give eyes a more tilted, defined shape.

quick.overview:
Winged eyeliner extends the line along the upper lashes past the outer corner of the eye. The payoff is a more upturned outer corner, the look of a positive canthal tilt, and a more defined eye shape, visible as soon as it is applied.

It is a long-standing makeup style that looksmaxxing communities discuss as a way to imitate canthal tilt. No published research was found on how it changes perceived eye tilt.
quick.how: A dark line is drawn along the upper lash line and flicked outward and upward, so the eye is visually extended in that direction. It is done with ordinary pencil or liquid liners, and the wing is typically drawn toward about the end of the eyebrow.
quick.risks: Eyeliner is a standard cosmetic with mainly irritation concerns. Product quality varies by region, and the FDA has described traditional kohl as unsafe because of lead.

angle.text: The wing is drawn outward and upward to suggest an upturned outer eye corner, giving the eyes a more tilted, defined shape as soon as it is applied. It is a standard makeup technique, and no formal studies of its effect on perceived tilt were found.

tightlining-waterline-liner.summary: Liner pressed against the lash roots or waterline to darken the lash line, making lashes look denser and eyes more defined.

quick.overview:
Tightlining is a makeup technique where liner is applied right against the lash roots, under the upper lashes and above the lower lashes. The payoff is a darker, denser lash line, fuller-looking lashes and eyes that look more defined and deeper-set.

Waterline liner is applied to the inner rim of the lid. Proponents in appearance communities say it suggests eye depth, and the technique can make lashes appear longer. No research was found on how it changes perceived eye shape or attractiveness.
quick.how: Dark pigment is worked into the gaps between lashes and along the lid margin. Waterproof products are usually preferred, and the look is visible immediately.
quick.risks: Liner at the lid margin sits very close to the eye surface, so irritation is the main general consideration. No studies on the technique were found.

angle.text: Liner placed at the lash roots or waterline makes the lashes look denser and the lash line darker, so the eyes look more defined and deeper-set as soon as it is applied. It is a popular makeup technique. Its effect on perceived eye depth has not been studied.

guyliner-kohl.summary: Eyeliner or kohl worn by men to darken the eye line for a more intense, defined gaze.

quick.overview:
Guyliner is eyeliner worn by men, and kohl, a soft dark powder, is among the oldest eye cosmetics, worn by Egyptian men and women of all classes. The payoff is stronger contrast around the eye, so the gaze looks darker, more intense and more defined.

The term became popular in the early 2000s emo scene. In appearance forums men's liner is discussed for a more intense or hunter-eyed look. No research was found on how liner changes perceived attractiveness in men.
quick.how: Dark pigment is placed along the lash line, which increases contrast and can make the eye look larger or more defined. Traditional kohl was made from stibnite or galena, while Western products generally use carbon or charcoal.
quick.risks: Studies since the early 1990s have found high lead levels in some kohl products, and lead exposure has been linked to anemia and developmental effects, though some research disputes the links. The FDA does not list kohl as an approved color additive and considers it unsafe, with import and sale in the US illegal. Western commercial eyeliners generally use other pigments.

angle.text: Men use eyeliner or kohl to make the eyes look darker and more intense, a visible change as soon as it is applied. The pigment raises contrast around the eye for a more defined gaze. The style runs from ancient Egyptian use to 2000s emo guyliner.

eyelash-growth-serum-peptide-otc.summary: Drug-free cosmetic serums applied along the lash line to make lashes look longer and fuller, sold as alternatives to prescription lash products.

quick.overview:
Peptide lash serums are over-the-counter products applied to the lash line, aimed at longer, thicker, fuller lashes that frame the eyes. They are often positioned as non-prescription alternatives to prescription bimatoprost (Latisse), a prostaglandin analogue.

Lashes differ from scalp hair: their length is largely genetically set, follicle number cannot increase after birth, and length, thickness and darkness decline with age. Some brands use peptides instead of prostaglandins because of regulatory rules in places such as Canada and California. No published human trials of the peptide products were found; trial data exist for bimatoprost.
quick.how: The serum is brushed along the base of the lashes, usually daily over weeks. Forum users ask for brand recommendations, report mixed results, and compare it with castor oil, rosemary oil, minoxidil and Latisse.
quick.risks: Safety data on specific peptide serums are limited. Eye-area products carry general irritation risks, and prescription bimatoprost has documented effects such as redness and eyelid darkening.

angle.text: Users apply these drug-free serums along the lash line hoping for longer, thicker lashes that frame the eyes and make them look fuller and more defined. They are sold as alternatives to prescription prostaglandin products. Trials exist for prescription bimatoprost, not for the peptide versions.

lash-extensions.summary: Salon-applied individual lashes bonded to your own for added length, curl and fullness, lasting a few weeks per set.

quick.overview:
Lash extensions are individual synthetic lashes attached by a technician to your own lashes. They add length, curl and fullness, so eyes look larger and more defined from the moment they are applied.

Styles are commonly classic (the most natural), volume (the fullest) and hybrid (a mix), with material, length, colour and curvature chosen to suit the eyes. An application can take up to two hours and lasts about three to four weeks depending on care.
quick.how: Each extension is bonded to a single natural lash with cyanoacrylate-type adhesive and falls out as the natural lash sheds. Users return to the salon for fills every few weeks to keep the look.
quick.risks: Case reports have linked the adhesive fumes to occupational asthma and rhinitis in technicians. Licensing rules vary by jurisdiction, and few clinical studies examine client outcomes.

angle.text: Lash extensions give longer, fuller, curled lashes that make the eyes look larger and more defined, visible as soon as they are applied. A set typically lasts a few weeks. The result is cosmetic and directly observable.

lash-tint.summary: Salon dye that darkens lashes so they look fuller and more defined without mascara.

quick.overview:
Lash tinting darkens eyelashes with dye so they look fuller and the eyes more defined without mascara. It is a common salon service, and the colour holds for several weeks.

Wikipedia lists tints alongside extensions among popular salon eyelash procedures. No published clinical studies of lash tinting were identified.
quick.how: A dye is applied to the lashes in a salon and stains the hair itself, so the colour lasts until the lashes shed. Users book repeat visits to maintain it and skip mascara day to day.
quick.risks: In the United States the FDA says hair dyes should not be used on eyelashes or eyebrows and that no color additives are approved for that use, citing reports of eye injuries, including blindness, from dyes used near the eyes.

angle.text: Lash tinting dyes the lashes darker so they look fuller and the eyes look more defined without mascara, a visible change that lasts several weeks. It is a common salon service. The effect is cosmetic and directly observable.

eyebrow-growth-serum.summary: Peptide and botanical serums applied to sparse brows to make them look denser and fuller.

quick.overview:
Eyebrow growth serums are topical products, often containing peptides or botanical extracts, sold to make sparse brows look denser and fuller. Fuller brows frame the eyes and strengthen the upper face.

In looksmaxxing communities they are discussed alongside castor oil, microneedling, minoxidil and prescription prostaglandin analogues. Published work centres on prescription bimatoprost applied to brows, while a 2019 paper reported on a plant-derived extract (Jarilla-Coffea) described as improving eyelash and eyebrow growth in women. No trials of peptide serums for brows were found.
quick.how: The serum is applied to the brows, usually once or twice daily over a period of weeks to months. Users often combine it with castor oil, microneedling or minoxidil. Makers and forum users describe peptides as stimulating follicle activity.
quick.risks: Eye-area products can irritate. Bimatoprost, a prescription drug, has its own documented effects such as eyelid darkening, and findings from bimatoprost studies do not carry over to peptide serums.

angle.text: Users apply peptide or botanical serums to make sparse brows look denser and fuller, often alongside castor oil, microneedling or minoxidil. The idea is that the serum stimulates the brow follicles. Published work centres on prescription bimatoprost rather than over-the-counter products.

castor-oil-on-brows-lashes.summary: Folk remedy of brushing castor oil onto brows and lashes to make them look thicker and longer.

quick.overview:
Castor oil is a thick plant oil pressed from castor beans, made mostly of triglycerides with ricinoleic acid as the main fatty acid. People brush it onto brows and lashes as a folk remedy for thicker, longer hair, and it is popular online.

Forum users report both positive and underwhelming results. Proponents attribute effects to ricinoleic acid and the oil's conditioning; no clinical study of the practice on brows or lashes was identified.
quick.how: A small amount is brushed onto the brows or the lash base, often at night with a clean spoolie or applicator, over weeks. It is commonly used alongside other brow and lash routines.
quick.risks: Topical use is generally described as low risk, but eye-area products can irritate, and the oil should be kept out of the eyes.

angle.text: Practitioners brush castor oil onto brows and lashes as a folk remedy for thicker, longer hair that frames the eyes. Proponents credit its ricinoleic acid and conditioning effect, and it is popular online. Use is driven by user reports rather than trials.
